forests.name: Mau Forest Complex
forests.biodiversity: Kenya's largest indigenous forest. Critical water tower — source of 12 rivers including Mara, Sondu Miriu, Njoro. Home to endangered Bongo antelope.

forests.name: Mount Kenya Forest Reserve
forests.biodiversity: UNESCO World Heritage Site. Afro-alpine moorlands above 3,000m. Elephants, buffalo, leopard, black rhino. Rare endemic plants.

forests.name: Aberdare Forest Reserve
forests.biodiversity: Major water tower for Nairobi. Dense bamboo zones. Elephants, bongo, giant forest hog, black leopard.

forests.name: Arabuko-Sokoke Forest
forests.biodiversity: Largest remaining patch of East African coastal forest. Home to endemic Sokoke Scops Owl, Clarke's Weaver, Golden-rumped Elephant Shrew.

forests.name: Kakamega Forest
forests.biodiversity: Kenya's only tropical rainforest — easternmost fragment of the Congo basin forest. 380+ bird species, 400+ butterfly species, 7 primate species.

forests.name: Karura Forest
forests.biodiversity: Nairobi's urban forest lung. Managed by Kenya Forest Service and Friends of Karura. Popular for jogging, cycling, and picnics. Waterfalls, caves.

forests.name: Ngong Hills Forest
forests.biodiversity: Iconic hills overlooking Nairobi and the Rift Valley. Popular hiking destination. Reforestation efforts ongoing.

forests.name: Cherangani Hills Forest
forests.biodiversity: Kenya's 5th-largest water tower. Rich biodiversity. Important watershed for Turkwel and Kerio rivers.

forests.name: Shimba Hills Forest
forests.biodiversity: Coastal forest with endemic Sable Antelope. Sheldrick Falls. Adjacent to Shimba Hills National Reserve.

forests.name: Mount Elgon Forest
forests.biodiversity: Cross-border forest with Uganda. Caves with salt-licking elephants. Giant lobelia and groundsel above 3,500m.

forests.name: Nandi Forest
forests.biodiversity: Important habitat for Nandi Bear (African Golden Cat). Rich bird diversity. Tea zone buffer forest.

forests.name: Meru Forest Reserve
forests.biodiversity: Cedar and camphor forests. Important watershed for Tana River tributaries.

forests.name: Marmanet Forest
forests.biodiversity: Transition forest between highland and semi-arid. Important water catchment for Ewaso Nyiro.

forests.name: South Nandi Forest
forests.biodiversity: Contiguous with North Nandi forest. Guinea-Congo biome relict. Important for primates.

forests.name: Kieni Forest
forests.biodiversity: Buffer forest for Mt. Kenya. Important elephant corridor between Mt. Kenya and Aberdares.

forests.name: Kaptagat Forest
forests.biodiversity: Training ground for Kenya's world-famous long-distance runners. Mixed indigenous and plantation forest.

forests.name: Londiani Forest
forests.biodiversity: Mau Forest complex fragment. Cypress and pine plantations with indigenous undergrowth.

forests.name: Turbo Forest
forests.biodiversity: Small but important catchment forest for Nzoia River system.

forests.name: Menengai Forest
forests.biodiversity: Forest on the rim of Menengai Crater. Scenic views. Geothermal activity below.

forests.name: Loita Forest
forests.biodiversity: Maasai community forest (not fully gazetted). Important wildlife corridor for Maasai Mara ecosystem.

ecosystemTypes.description: Highland forests above 1,500m. Dominated by cedar, camphor, olive, and bamboo. Kenya's major water towers.
Equatorial forest with year-round rainfall. Only found at Kakamega in Kenya. Highest biodiversity.
Tropical dry and moist forests along the coast. Unique biodiversity including many endemic species.
High-altitude vegetation above 3,000m on Mt. Kenya and Mt. Elgon. Giant lobelia and groundsel.
Transition forests between humid highlands and semi-arid lowlands. Important catchment areas.
Gazetted forests within urban areas. Critical for air quality, recreation, and urban biodiversity.

notes: Kenya has approximately 1,200 gazetted forest reserves covering about 7.4% of land area. This directory covers the most significant ones.
Data sourced from Kenya Forest Service (KFS) and Kenya Forest Research Institute (KEFRI) publications.
Kenya's '5 Water Towers' (Mt. Kenya, Aberdares, Mau, Cherangani, Mt. Elgon) supply 75% of Kenya's surface water.
Hiking in gazetted forests requires a KFS permit. Fees: KES 250 (citizen), KES 600 (resident), USD 20 (non-resident) per day.
Report illegal logging or charcoal burning to KFS hotline: 0800 723 253 (toll-free).
